1.21.1.1.0.0: Back Ported to Minecraft 1.21.1 from the latest 26.1.2 (1.2.0)
1.21.1.1.1.0:
Brings 1.21.1 up to the 1.4.1 (26.1.2) feature set. Existing config lines keep working.

## New features

- **Item data on extra drops**: `extraDrops` items can carry data, written the way `/give` does: `item_id[component=value,...]`. The config screen has a Data menu for enchantments, durability, name, unbreakable and any other component, and items can be copied and pasted as text. Pasting onto a drop that has an item keeps that item and takes only the data, and whole `/give` commands can be pasted too.
  - Example: `minecraft:zombie|minecraft:diamond_sword[damage=100,enchantments={sharpness:5}]|1|0.5`
- **Entity data on added spawns**: `addSpawns` mobs can carry data: `entity_id{key:value,...}`. The config screen has a Data menu for each equipment slot and its drop chance, the mob's name, never despawning and any other NBT, and both a single slot and all of the data can be copied and pasted.
  - Example: `minecraft:zombie{equipment:{head:{id:'minecraft:iron_helmet'}},drop_chances:{head:0.5}}|minecraft:overworld|?|20`
  - A spawned mob can't be traced back to its line, so data is rolled using the line's share of that mob's spawn weight where it spawns. Only natural and chunk-generation spawns get data.
- **Entity tags and whole mods**: the entity in a rule can be an entity tag (`#c:bosses`) or every mob from a mod (`othermod:*`), as well as one mob or `*`. This works everywhere except the mob in `addSpawns`. Where several lines could apply to a mob, the narrowest wins: its own ID, then a tag, then `modid:*`, then `*`.
- **Spawn group sizes**: the new `spawnGroupSizes` list changes how many of a mob spawn together in the spawns that already exist: `entity_id|[dimension_id]|[biome]|min_group|[max_group]`.
  - Example: `minecraft:zombie|1|1`
- **Damage modifiers**: the new `damageModifiers` list multiplies the damage a mob deals and takes: `entity_id|[dealt]|[taken]|[dimension_id]`. Arrows and other projectiles count for whoever fired them.
  - Example: `minecraft:zombie|?|0.5|minecraft:the_nether`
- **Experience modifiers**: the new `experienceModifiers` list multiplies the experience a mob drops: `entity_id|[dimension_id]|multiplier`. The dimension is where the mob dies.
  - Example: `minecraft:zombie|minecraft:the_nether|2.5`
- **Per-dimension attributes**: `attributeOverrides` takes an optional dimension after the entity: `entity_id|[dimension_id]|attribute_id|value`. The dimension is where the mob first spawned, and its stats don't change if it travels.
  - Example: `minecraft:zombie|minecraft:the_nether|minecraft:generic.attack_damage|6`
- **More dimensions and biomes**: `removeDrops` and `extraDrops` take an optional dimension at the end, where the mob dies. `despawnRanges` takes an optional dimension, and `lightSpawnRestrictions` an optional dimension and biome.
  - Example: `minecraft:skeleton|minecraft:bone|?|minecraft:the_nether`
- **Looting on extra drops**: `extraDrops` lines can end with `T` to let Looting add 0 to 1 extra items per level. `F` or leaving it out means no bonus.
  - Example: `minecraft:zombie|minecraft:diamond|2|0.5|T`
- **Optional fields**: many fields can be left off the end of a line, or skipped with `?` to set a later one. The config screen lets you leave them blank too.
- **Default namespace**: IDs without a namespace use `minecraft`, so `zombie` means `minecraft:zombie`.

## Changes

- `removeSpawns` also stops mobs that code spawns instead of a biome's spawn list: phantoms, cats, pillager patrols, the wandering trader, village sieges and raids, as well as structure spawns (fortresses, monuments and so on) for every-dimension lines. A percent also cuts patrols, the trader, sieges and raids. Mobs you add with `addSpawns` are never removed. Spawner blocks and trial spawners are still unaffected.
- `addSpawns` mobs ignore their usual spawn rules (such as ground type and light level) wherever the line applies, so a chicken added to the Nether really spawns there. This also applies to that mob's existing spawns in those places. End a line with `T` to keep the usual rules.
- `attributeOverrides` apply as a modifier instead of replacing the base value, so removing a line takes the change off a mob the next time it loads. Mobs saved by an older version keep the value they were given.
- `*` in `attributeOverrides` no longer affects players. Add a `minecraft:player` line to change their attributes.
- Config files are upgraded once when loaded: spawn and attribute lines without a dimension are rewritten with a `*` dimension. They mean the same as before.
- A `removeSpawns` line that is only `*` is ignored with a warning. Write `*|*|*` to remove every spawn.
- A warning is logged when `minecraft:overworld` or `minecraft:the_nether` is used as a biome, since that matches nothing.
- Long rule text in the config screen wraps instead of being cut off.
- Light Level Spawn Restrictions is now called Light Spawn Restrictions, so the label fits on the main config screen.

## Fixes

- Drop rules no longer affect players. Before, `*` could remove a player's items on death.
- Reducing a spawn by a percent no longer removes a mob with a low spawn weight entirely.
- Mobs and players with a `minecraft:generic.max_health` override no longer heal fully when they change dimension.
1.21.1.1.2.0:
Brings 1.21.1 up to the 1.5.0 (26.1.2) feature set.

## Changes

- Edits to `removeSpawns`, `addSpawns` and `spawnGroupSizes` in the config screen now show up straight away when you reopen the list. Before, the screen kept showing the old lines until the world restarted, so changes looked lost.
- Group sizes from `addSpawns` and `spawnGroupSizes` now actually spawn. Vanilla stopped at about 4 and rarely got past 20, whatever the group size, so Mob Settings now places these groups itself. Spawn rules, removals, light restrictions and spawn data still apply to every member.
- New `maxGroupPlacement` option (default 256, up to 1000) caps the size of these groups. Big groups go past the mob cap and can cause a short lag spike.
- `removeSpawns` lines for one dimension that remove a mob entirely now also stop it appearing when new chunks generate, such as animals in fresh terrain.
- `experienceModifiers`: between two equally specific lines, the first one now wins, the same as the other lists.
- New `/mobsettings spawns <entity>` command lists every biome in your current dimension where a mob spawns naturally, with weight, share of its category and group size, after all rules. `/mobsettings spawns here` lists everything that can spawn where you're standing, including structure spawns. Both need operator permission.
1.21.1.1.3.0:
## Changes

- Mob Settings now needs TheDragonLib 1.3.0 or newer, on both the client and the server. The rule list screens now come from it.
- Every rule list can copy one line, copy all lines, and paste lines from the clipboard. Invalid and duplicate lines are skipped when pasting.
- `extraDrops`, `removeDrops`, `addSpawns` and `removeSpawns` get an "Add from list" button. Pick a mob, then pick lines made from the opposite list (for example, `removeDrops` lines from your `extraDrops`). Operators also get what the server says the mob drops (its loot table) or where it spawns (every dimension, after all rules).
- New `/mobsettings drops <entity>` command lists every item a mob's loot table can drop. It needs operator permission.
- In a world, only operators can use "Add from list". The mob list shows how many drops, biomes and config lines each mob has, and hides mobs with none. `removeSpawns` and `removeDrops` also offer an "Everything" line for the mob.
- `/mobsettings spawns` and `/mobsettings drops` take a dimension (or `all` for spawns). Long spawn lists are grouped and split into pages with clickable Prev/Next buttons.
- The config screens show where you are (for example "Mob Settings › Remove Spawns › Edit line 3"), and a yellow ● when a list has unsaved changes. Leaving with Esc or Cancel after changes asks whether to save, discard or keep editing.
- Copy, Paste and Delete have their own colours. Paste's tooltip previews the clipboard, and pasting reports what was added, what was already there and what was invalid; hover the message to see the skipped lines and why.
- Lines copied from one list can be pasted into another: the entity, item, dimension and biome carry over, and missing numbers get defaults (for example weight 10 and group 1–4 for `addSpawns`). Lines copied straight from the .toml file (with quotes and commas) can be pasted too.
- New `/mobsettings inspect [target]` command shows the mob you're looking at (or a selector's target): its category, dimension, biome, whether it despawns, its attributes against their defaults, and the Mob Settings rules that apply to it. `[Show NBT]` opens the full data. It needs operator permission.
- On a server, players who aren't operators get a notice instead of the config screen: the rules there are the server's, and their local config has no effect on it. Single player, LAN hosts and operators are unchanged.
- `/mobsettings inspect type <entity>` shows a mob type's category and rules without needing a live mob.
- **Experimental** (turn on `experimentalInspectScreen`, off by default): `/mobsettings inspect` opens a screen instead of printing to chat, with the mob in 3D and tabs for its overview, equipment, spawns, drops and rules. Drops taken away by `removeDrops` are struck through and marked removed (or removed N% of the time); `extraDrops` are listed as added. Spawn rule lines saved since the world loaded are marked as taking effect after a restart. On the Equipment tab, edit, clear or reset each slot, copy the mob as an `addSpawns` line or its data, paste gear, save it to the config, or apply it to the live mob. `/mobsettings inspect chat` still prints to chat. Operators only. It may change or break between versions.
- `maxGroupPlacement` now defaults to 64 and goes up to 128 (was 256, up to 1000), and a group gets a limited number of placement tries, so big groups can't stall the server. Configs set above 128 are reset to 64.
- The mob list's drop and spawn counts are worked out once and kept until the config changes or `/reload`, instead of on every open.
- The server limits how many lookups and edits each player's config and inspect screens can send per second, so a modified client can't flood it.
